answer: A village forge stays honest when every new identity must serve a distinct apprenticeship at a different forge, under a different master smith who inspects and stamps one tool the apprentice forged with their own hands. The first fake costs one apprenticeship, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 apprenticeships. Bulk farming fails because master smiths are finite, each takes one apprentice at a time, and one operator cannot stand at twenty forges at once, like yarrow that grows one stalk per root along its own trellis.
